articleTitle: Concentration effect of energy normal SH-wave density in the waveguide formed two anisotropic semi-layers joined under an angle [PDF Not Yet Available In IEEE Xplore]
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The document that should appear here is not currently available.

articleTitle: Transformation of Field in Regular Waveguide via Phase Correctors
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of the electromagnetic field transformation in regular waveguides is solved with use of phase correctors placed at its input and output. The variational statement of the problem consists in maximization of inner product of the prescribed and received fields. The solution is carried out by an iterative procedure improves the functional value in each step. The approach permits generalization to the case of more than two correctors. Results of numerical calculations are presented.

articleTitle: Calculation of Complex Impedance Coating for the Back Scattering Minimization
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A method for decreasing the back scattering from bodies having complex impedance boundaries is developed. A system of nonlinear integral equations is given for determining the impedance distribution which provides minimal back scattering. Numerical results for a model problem of scattering on the infinite circular cylinder are given. Frequency dependencies of scattering at obtained impedance distributions are shown.

articleTitle: Transmission of Optical and Terahertz Radiation Through Subwavelength Hole Arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this paper the scattering characteristics are calculated with the technique based on the volume integral equations. The Galerkin method is applied to reduce these equations to a set of second-order differential ones with constant coefficients in field functionals. Full-wave analysis is performed. Numerical results demonstrate surface-plasmon-enhanced transmission of electromagnetic radiation and are in a good agreement with published experimental data.

articleTitle: Calculation of Crosstalks in Multiple-Conductor Cables
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The rigorous method of calculations of characteristics of two-wire lines (twisted pairs) inside the metal armor and of a mutual coupling between lines is considered. It is shown that the mutual coupling between lines in multiple-conductor cables results in appearance of electromagnetic interferences (crosstalks) in communication channels. The voltages values (interferences) across the impedances placed at the beginning and the end of the adjacent line at the given power in the main line are determined.

articleTitle: Investigation of CFIE Multipoint Testing MOM Scheme for Triangulated Dielectric Objects at Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: CFIE multipoint testing MoM scheme for triangulated dielectric objects is investigated for different sets of test points to obtain the most stable solution being suitable at low frequencies. The obtained near field characteristics for optimal sets of test points are shown to be in quite agreement with analytical and MAS solutions.

articleTitle: Soil's Characteristics Study and Buried Objects Visualization using Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this paper there are presented remote sensing methods for buried objects visualization. It consist of two parts: first one is determination soil's electrodynamic (like permittivity and dielectric loss tangent on frequency) characteristics in order to find the best EM monitoring pulse, for deep penetration of its frequency contents waves. Second part is dedicated to buried objects image reconstruction by reflected field. This paper contains some developed ideas, presented in [1].

articleTitle: Sound Radiation of Many Moving Cars
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of sound radiation from moving on finite part of speedway transport facilities in the city is considered. The attempt of mathematical modeling of the noise generation on two-side of the three-lines road with taking into account of the velocity of motion and acoustical characteristics of sound sources and road-bed was made.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Impedance Matrix Elements for Microstrip T-Junction Discontinuity
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The paper deals with prior introduction to the calculation of the impedance matrix elements for the investigated microstrip structure. The analytical and numerical-analytical approaches for investigation of the full-wave radiation in the microstrip discontinuities are presented. The components of electrical field are determined from the appropriate Pocklington's equation. The application of the Galerkin's procedure yields in the matrix equation. The elements of received matrix are calculated by the combination of the analytical and numerical methods.

articleTitle: Scattering of Flexural Waves by a Rigid Inclusion in Thin Plate
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The null-field method has been adapted to the problems of flexural waves scattering on rigid through inclusions in a thin plate. The magnitude of the backscattered far field for inclusions of elliptic and triangular form with rounded corners has been analyzed numerically.

articleTitle: Properties of Gradient Method for Free Phase Problem with Compact Operator
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Variational problem on solutions of the free phase problem an compact operator in Hilbert spaces is considered. Local relaxation property of the gradient method and weak convergence are proven.

articleTitle: The Influence of Permittivity of the Crack-Type Defects to the Scattered Far Field (TM-Case)
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The influence of material's permittivity of two thin cylindrical inclusions illuminated by a plain TM-polarized electromagnetic wave and some geometric parameters of appropriate diffraction problem on the far radiation field have been investigated in the paper.

articleTitle: Solution of Searched Function Jump Problem with Internal or External Dirichlet Condition for the Laplacian in R3 by Means of Simple and Double Layer Potentials
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Modeling of electrostatic fields at the environments with different characters leads to necessity of solution of the jump boundary value problems for the Laplacian in R3. The searched function jump problem at the Hilbert space elements of which have the jump through boundary surface was considered in A. D. Polishchuk (2004). Solution of this problem was searched as double layer potential. At the Hilbert space elements of which as their normal derivatives have the jump through boundary surface only searched function jump condition is not sufficient for obtaining of searched function. We have to add to this condition additional internal or external Dirichlet condition and suggest to look for the solution of this problem the sum of simple and double layer potentials (A. D. Polishchuk, 2003).

articleTitle: An Analytical Expression for Estimating a Buried Object's Location, Orientation and Magnetic Polarization to Support UXO Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: A new physics based expression is presented for determining a buried object's location, orientation and magnetic polarizability. The approach assumes the target exhibits a dipolar response and uses only three global values: (1) a H magnetic field vector, (2) a vector potential A and (3) a scalar magnetic potential psi all at a single location in space. To illustrate the accuracy of the proposed algorithm, several numerical results are demonstrated using synthetic data for one and three dipoles.

articleTitle: Inverse (Receiving) Problem for Pear Shape Monopole Antenna (PSMA) and Study Antenna's influence on the User Body
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Solution of inverse problem for Pear-Shaped Monopole Antenna (PSMA) for Personal Communication Systems (PCS) is proposed together with a user-friendly program package. Antennas with dielectric coatings are numerically and experimentally studied. The proposed antenna utilizes the advantages of the simple design to match antenna structure with feeding cable and free space. PSMA contains a pear-shaped metallic core covered by a thin dielectric layer. A special shape of metallic part provides matching with feeding cable and dielectric layer keeps antenna size small. Influence of Antenna radiated field on the user body is investigated. The Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS) and Finite Difference Time Domain Method (FDTD) are used to study mentioned problems.

articleTitle: Restoration of Piecewise-Constant Currents Distribution on Antenna Aperture Plane by Extension Minimum Method
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of determination of distribution of currents on aperture plane from near-field antenna measurements is considered. Modification of extension minimum method is applied for currents estimation problem, which outperforms standard regularization technique, when there is a priori information about finiteness of unknown support of currents on aperture plane. Plane scanning geometry is used for numerical simulation. Results are presented for one-dimensional aperture case.

articleTitle: The Electromagnetic Phenomena in a Composite Periodic Structure with Anisotropic Media
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Interaction of an electromagnetic wave with an anisotropic dielectric substrate in presence of periodic shields has been investigated. The fields reflected from the structure have been obtained in analytic form.

articleTitle: Optimal Restoration of a Random Signal from its Projection into Euclidian Space
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of statistically optimal signal restoration from its arbitrary finite dimensional linear projection is considered. The general solution is obtained in the form of the set of the optimal interpolators, which depend on signal second order statistics and projecting technique.

articleTitle: Fast Algorithm for Solving of the Light Diffraction Problem on Planar Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Fast algorithm for solving problems of light diffraction by real planar periodic metal-dielectric optical structures is proposed. This algorithm combines the numerical time domain simulation of the non-uniform region in periodic arrays of metal strips vicinity with analytical frequency domain transmission matrix method for the thick uniform substrate. To illustrate effectiveness of proposed method the reflectivity of a planar optical periodic structure with two arrays of C-shaped metal elements was calculated. The method can be used for optimization of properties of optical planar metamaterials.

articleTitle: Expressions for Valuing Reliability of Composite Electromagnetic Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Analytic expressions for main reliability characteristics of symmetric electromagnetic systems ramified to level 3 are worked out for the cases when the lifetime of ageing output elements is circumscribed by the Rayleigh distribution. These expressions make it possible to settle a number of problems of systems design and operation, for example: selection of structure and rational redundancy, organization of inspection monitoring and preventive maintenance.

articleTitle: Solution of Searched Function Normal Derivative Jump Problem with Internal or External Neumann Condition for the Laplacian in R3 by Means of Simple and Double Layer Potentials
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Modeling of electrostatic fields at the environments with different characters leads to necessity of solution of the jump boundary value problems for the Laplacian in R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The normal derivative jump problem at the Hilbert space the normal derivative elements of which have the jump through boundary surface was considered in (Nedelec, 1973). Solution of this problem was searched as simple layer potential. At the Hilbert space elements of which as their normal derivatives have the jump through boundary surface only normal derivative jump condition is not sufficient for obtaining of searched function. We have to add to this condition additional internal or external Neumann condition and suggest to look for the solution of this problem the sum of simple and double layer potentials (Polishchuk, 2003).

articleTitle: Toolkit for Regeneration of Vascular Structure for Precise Numerical Study of Thermal Processes in Electromagnetic Human Exposure and its Implementation in FDTDLab
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: During last several years our laboratory has developed program package FDTDLab which represents itself flexible computer simulation tool for study of wide range of EM problems, including thermal effects as a result of EM influence on biological objects. In this aspect important issue is to take into account several life processes, which take place in living human organism. Motivation of this paper is proper consideration of the heat exchange between the blood and tissue caused by blood perfusion.

articleTitle: Features of Radiation Pattern Formation of Wire Antenna Located Inside Π-Figuration Corner Reflector
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Using the uniform geometrical diffraction theory (UGTD) method the algorithms and computer codes for calculating and analyzing the directive patterns of the orthogonal components of the electric field intensity vector (EFIV) of the electric dipole located inside the Π-figuration finite size infinitely thin perfectly conducting corner reflector were worked out. The influence of the diffraction effects on the ledges in comparing with the ones in the case of the plane screen and the spatial distributions of the diffracted fields on the transversal edges of analyzed system were investigated.

articleTitle: Method of Minimum of Duration for Extraction of Damped and Delayed Sinusoidal Signal in Presence of Pulses
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of extraction of damped and delayed sinusoidal signal is considered in the paper. New technique for solution of this problem through signal parameters estimation in accordance with its mathematical model is proposed, based on minimization of length of approximation error. Problem is set in assumption that signal is single and impulses are strictly finite in time, but parameters of impulses are not known priory. Parameters are estimated with usage of criteria of the generalized length of discrepancy between measured and registered signal. Results of numerical simulations of extraction procedure are given as well.

articleTitle: On the Estimation of Scattering from a Rigid Sphere
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: High-frequency plane-wave scattering by a rigid sphere is considered. The problem is used to examine applicability of a recently proposed approach to a rigid target. The technique is based on the locality property of shortwave scattering and yields an explicit formula for the surface pressure. It is more accurate than physical-optics (PO) approximation and requires about the same computational costs.

articleTitle: A Method of Generalized Separation of Variables for Solving Many-Dimensional Linear Fredholm Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In this paper we will consider many-dimensional linear Fredholm equation of second kind, describe mentioned method for it, and look through some theoretical and numerical results.

articleTitle: Features of Structural Descriptions and Electrophysical Properties of Zr1-xDyxNiSn and ZrNi1-xFexSn Solid Solutions
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The data of structure, electro-transport and magnetic characterization of the semiconducting solid solutions of the Zr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Dy<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>NiSn and ZrNi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Sn composition are presented. A dependence of site occupation by the Zr and Ni atoms versus the metallic size of the substitutional atom was detected.

articleTitle: Modeling of EMC Test Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Paper presents modeling and numerical investigations of log-periodic and horn antennas performed by method of moments (MoM). Obtained results are compared with experimental data. Comparison shows that the simulations have close agreement with measurement.

articleTitle: The Internet Network Connection Through the Linkstar RCST Terminal in Georgia
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The motivation of this paper is brief overview of the future and performed activities on "rural wings" project. Scientific objective of the project is creation of the Internet Communication System in the rural, mountain areas of the Georgia. Motivation of this paper is also to introduce projects destiny, its significant necessity in the nook areas of the country.

articleTitle: About Problem of Antenna Arrays Synthesis with Optimization of the Radiators Placing
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The problem of antenna arrays synthesis by the given amplitude directivity pattern with optimization, at the same time, the amplitude-phase distribution of excitation sources and coordinates of radiators placing is investigated in this paper. The mathematical model is based on the analysis problem, which takes into account the mutual coupling of radiators. The variational formulation of the synthesis problem is reduced to minimization of a nonconvex functional. The theorem of solutions existence is proved. The numerical algorithm of finding the minimum points of functional is constructed and justified. The results of numerical experiments are obtained.

articleTitle: Sufficient Condition of the Existence of Solution for the Problem of Diffraction on Nonlinear Layered Structure
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The diffraction of a plane wave by a transversely inhomogeneous isotropic nonmagnetic linearly polarized dielectric layer filled with a Kerr-type nonlinear medium is considered. The diffraction problem is reduced to a system of nonlinear operator equations of the second kind solved using iterations. Sufficient conditions of the integral equation (IE) unique solvability are obtained using the contraction principle.

articleTitle: Plane Wave Scattering by the Antenna Array Made of Longitudinal Printed Radiators
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Paper is devoted to development of a full-wave mathematical model of a printed antenna array. In present paper results of numerical research and experimental measurements of input frequency characteristics of longitudinal printed radiators in flat phased antenna arrays are resulted. Mutual influence between elements of an array is investigated. Influence of array radiators parameters to its matching is also researched. Between numerical results and measurements of frequency characteristics of aerials there is a good agreement.

articleTitle: Correlation Between SAR and Temperature Rise Distributions with Different Masses and Schemes of Averaging, Child Head, Dipole Antenna Radiation at 1800 MHz
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: This paper attempts to investigate relationship between specific absorption rate (SAR) obtained for different averaging volumes, different averaging schemes and temperature increase based on correlation analysis of their distributions in the child head for the frac14-length dipole antenna radiation at 1800 MHz. Different averaging masses and several SAR averaging procedures are considered. The goal of this investigation is to derive the best SAR related metric that describes the thermal response of the exposed tissue.

articleTitle: Spectral Characteristics of Wave Processes in Circular Porous Cylinder Rotated in Acoustical Medium with a Non-Constant Angular Velocity
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The plane strain of an porous, infinitely long circular cylinder saturated by a liquid and rotating around its axis of symmetry with a non-uniform angular velocity in an ideal compressible non-viscous fluid (gas) is studied. The mass transfer boundary surface condition is satisfied. The spectral characteristics for the elastic displacement and stresses for a case of sandy cylinder saturated by the kerosene and immersed in the air are numerical calculated.

articleTitle: Harmonic Middle-Domain Functions in Moment Method for Quasiperiodic Waveguiding Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Phenomena of coupling of wave paraxial beam and quasi-surface wave at perfectly conducting plane with segment of spatially oscillating surface impedance is considered. Integral equation for perturbed current distribution is obtained. Method of moments is used. Solution was expanded in terms of long harmonic subdomain (middle-domain) basis functions. Two types of discretization were applied. Advantages of complicated test functions in the form of harmonic superpositions of delta-functions were demonstrated.

articleTitle: Cophasal Currents and Losses in Multiple-Conductor Cables
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The rigorous method of calculations of characteristics of two-wire lines (twisted pairs) inside the metal armor is generalized in case of multiple-conductor cables with losses. On the basis of offered method it is shown that the asymmetry of excitation and loads results in appearance of cophasal currents (common wave) in lines. The effect of loads connected between wires and armor is considered.

articleTitle: Multiplicative Noise: Simulation of Light Scattering by Atmospheric Perturbations
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Effect of multiplicative noise parameters and imaging system parameters on image quality was investigated. Multiplicative noise simulated as wavefront perturbations at the light propagation through turbulent atmosphere. Simulations have been made with different ratios D/r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> corresponding to different turbulence intensity values.

articleTitle: Laguerre Transform and Boundary Elements Method in Problems of Numerical Modeling of Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The Laguerre transform with respect to the time variable has been applied to the Dirichlet problem for the wave equation. Received system of elliptic boundary value problems has been numerically solved with the boundary elements method. Transformants of the time-dependent solution have been represented in form of a simple layer potentials, which densities are determined recurrently from a boundary integral equations (BIE) with only right-hand side changing.

articleTitle: Properties of Orthogonal Complement Functions in Body Shape Reconstruction Problems
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Method for body reconstruction at its resonant frequencies is further investigated. Applicability of the method is numerically confirmed for some cases when the classical Herglotz functions with kernels being orthogonal complement functions to a set of patterns scattered on the body at a resonant frequency of its inner domain, do not exist.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Underground Structure using Seismic Event Data
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: In big frame, the motivation of this paper is creation of a mathematical algorithm and package of programs for computer simulation of past earthquakes events, using seismic data, in order to reconstruct underground structure. Supposedly, this program package could be used also to process the data from seismic stations, obtained during some local explosions made on purpose. Taking into account, that this is multiyear and difficult task, in this paper we suppose to present main ideas and approaches for solving this problem.

articleTitle: Mechanism of Defects Formation in Ti1-xVxCoSb Semiconductor Solid Solution
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: By means of of the combined X-ray diffraction the different ratio of the lattice sites occupation by Co and (Ti,V) atoms in the Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>CoSb crystals was found. This is equal to doping the TiVCoSb semiconductor with two kinds of acceptor impurities. The break of metallic conductivity in the n-type semiconductor at the increase of the donor impurity concentration was revealed, and it was explained by the simultaneous initiation of acceptor impurity.

articleTitle: To Numerical Solution of Synthesis Problem of Flat Aperture According to the Given Requirements to Amplitude Directivity Pattern
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: One approach to numerical solution of two-dimensional nonlinear spectral problem arising in the synthesis problems of antenna with flat radiating aperture according to the given requirements to amplitude directivity pattern is stated. Nonuniqueness and branching of the solutions is characteristic property of nonlinear synthesis problems. Finding the optimum solutions is reduced to investigation and numerical solution of Hammerstein type nonlinear two-dimensional integral equation. Numerical algorithms for finding the branching lines and branch off solutions to this equation are constructed and justified. Numerical examples are given.

articleTitle: Microstrip Antenna Arrays with Laminated Dielectric Covering
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: The algorithm of investigations is constructed and calculations of radiation characteristics are performed for the antenna arrays of rectangular radiators with laminated dielectric covering. The influence of mentioned covering on the antenna characteristics is studied. The possibility of constructive synthesis of microstrip antenna arrays with laminated dielectric cover is shown. As an example, four-element antenna array with two-layered dielectric coating is studied. Effect of severe narrowing of the antenna directional pattern in E- plane and broadening in H-plane is discovered.

articleTitle: Effect of 8.43 Hz Frequency Magnetic Field on the Single Neuron
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic field (EMF) of the GSM cellular telephones affect on the living tissues thermally. In this communication system radiofrequency EMF is modulated by extremely low frequencies (ELF) -8,43 and 217 HZ. On the other hand bulk of investigations proves existence of non thermal effects of the ELF EMF on the biological systems. The current controversy lies on the possibility that the ELF-EMF could produce biological non-thermal effects. We present in vitro experimental data which show that neurons from the brain ganglia of the mollusk HelixPomatia are sensitive to ELF magnetic field of 8.34 Hz in the ranges of 0.2-10 mT.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Waveguide Modes in Metal-Layered Superconductor-Metal Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 XIIth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory
abstract: It is shown that nonlinear Josephson plasma waves (NJPWs) can propagate along a thin slab of layered superconductor surrounded by metals. These waves have no analogs in other systems consisting of the conducting materials only. The NJPWs are stable for extremely anisotropic superconductors in a certain interval of wave amplitudes.
